evidence: not-served-on-another-address: service.erb:10 binds gunicorn to <%= @ip_address %>:<%= @port %>; with the params fixture 127.0.0.1:8080 nothing listens on 10.0.2.15:8080, so curl rc 7 is what the line produces (and the invariant holds on the clean node)

finding the-agent-run-restores-the-unit-in-effect: after the second agent run the unit file is restored (grep count 1) but 8080 returns 000 and 8081 still answers (curl-rc=0): the service kept the hand-changed unit. The agent events show Exec[...-restart] Triggered before Exec[...-reload]; in the baseline both are refreshonly, both notified by the unit file (pp:28, 72) with no ordering between them, and manifest order puts restart (84) before daemon-reload (88), so the restart runs on the stale definition. A real upstream ordering defect against the class's own intent (pp:83 'restart and reload the service when the files change'), not a test artifact: a Puppet-driven unit change (new port/address) would hit the same order

purpose covered: Purpose (deploy a Flask welcome page under localdir, run it with gunicorn as systemd service on the given address/port, restart on file or unit change) matches the baseline manifest, its common class and both templates. Tested: service active+enabled, unit ExecStart/WorkingDirectory, page served with the configured message, not served on the other address, a hand change to the app restored and restarted by the agent run, a hand change to the unit restored and expected in effect (this last one is the finding). The mutating checks declare exactly their sed/daemon-reload/restart or HTTP-only effects, and their effects are read-only curl/grep of the result. Uncovered rows are honest: the RedHat ExecStart branch (service.erb:7-8) needs a set run on rhel9, and phase3.py picks the node only from the plan (nodes.select(cls=cls)), with no per-set or --node override, so the capability really is missing; uninstall/other address/port/message need more than one params fixture, and the runner applies one fixture per set. wsgi.py's notify uses the same $files_notify path that the app-file check exercises.
